title: Multi-agent failure modes
summary: MAST, a failure taxonomy built from real traces, groups 14 failure modes into system design issues, inter-agent misalignment and task verification. Most are visible in traces if you look for them.
useIf: You are reviewing, debugging or evaluating a multi-agent system and need a checklist of how such systems actually fail.
avoidIf: You have one agent with no handoffs. A multi-agent taxonomy then adds little, and single-agent loop failures matter more.

explain.md: *Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?* introduces **MAST**, the Multi-Agent System Failure Taxonomy. The authors built it from 150 traces with expert annotators (inter-annotator agreement kappa 0.88), then released **MAST-Data**, more than 1,600 annotated traces from 7 multi-agent frameworks, plus an LLM-as-a-judge annotator. The taxonomy has 14 failure modes in 3 categories. The paper was first submitted on 2025-03-17 and revised on 2025-10-26 [[r5]]. Its opening observation is that performance gains from multi-agent systems on popular benchmarks are often minimal, so understanding failures matters.

explain.md: The verification finding is the most actionable. The paper describes a generated chess program that passed superficial checks even though the verifier was prompted to be thorough, and argues for more rigorous verification with external knowledge and collected test output [[r5]]. This matches Cognition's report that a review loop works best when the reviewer shares no context with the coder [[r4]] and Anthropic's advice to resume from checkpoints because errors compound in stateful agents [[r2]]. Treat the taxonomy as a review checklist: sample traces, label them by mode, and fix the largest bucket first. The authors' LLM judge can automate labelling, but you still calibrate it against your own annotations.

explain.title: Read the numbers with care
explain.md: Frequencies in the paper depend on the frameworks, models and tasks sampled. Use the modes as a vocabulary for your own traces, not as universal rates.

pitfalls.symptom: The run reports success and a spot check fails
pitfalls.cause: No or incomplete verification, a task verification failure [[r5]]
pitfalls.fix: Add an independent verifier with a clean context and an external check such as tests or a schema.

pitfalls.symptom: Agents repeat steps or never stop
pitfalls.cause: Unaware of termination conditions, a system design failure [[r5]]
pitfalls.fix: Put termination rules, hop caps and budgets in the harness and make them visible to agents.

pitfalls.symptom: Agent B acts without a fact agent A already found
pitfalls.cause: Information withholding or loss of history between agents
pitfalls.fix: Pass structured state or artifact references, and share full traces instead of summaries [[r3]].

scenarios.title: Success reported, results wrong
scenarios.situation: A multi-agent pipeline reports completion on most tasks, but spot checks find that a sizeable share of outputs do not meet the spec. A reviewer agent exists, and it nearly always approves.
constraints: A reviewer agent shares the generator's context
Spec can be partly checked by code
unknowns: What share of failures does the reviewer miss on a labelled sample?
Which spec items can be tested in code?
scenarios.question: What do you fix first?

options.name: Replace the shared-context reviewer with an independent verifier that runs external checks, and calibrate it on labelled failures
options.why: This targets the verification category directly, and independence plus external evidence catches what a same-context reviewer approves.
options.tradeoff: More cost per run and effort to build checks and a labelled set.

options.name: Add more agents to the pipeline
options.why: It adds coordination faults without fixing the missing verification.
options.tradeoff: Right only when a specific capability is missing and measured.

options.name: Tighten the generator prompts
options.why: Cheap and may reduce some spec violations.
options.tradeoff: It does not detect failures, so wrong outputs still pass.

flips.then: Fix message structure and shared state before verification.

flips.if: A single agent passes the same evals

scenarios.title: Where do we start with a failing crew?
scenarios.situation: A team's agent crew fails often and the causes look scattered. They have 500 traces, a judge model they trust somewhat, and one engineer-week.
unknowns: How well does the judge agree with human labels on a small sample?
scenarios.question: How do you spend the week?

options.name: Hand-label about fifty traces with the taxonomy, calibrate the judge on them, label the rest and fix the biggest bucket
options.why: It builds a vocabulary and a checked labeller, then aims effort at the largest bucket.
options.tradeoff: Up-front annotation effort, and rates will reflect your system only.

options.name: Trust the judge on all 500 traces without calibration
options.why: Uncalibrated judges can mislabel systematically, so you may fix the wrong thing.
options.tradeoff: Acceptable once agreement with human labels is measured.

options.name: Rewrite every agent prompt
options.tradeoff: No diagnosis, so you cannot tell which change helped.

flips.if: Judge agreement with humans is high
flips.then: Label all traces with it and sample for audit.
Fix it first regardless of frequency.

scenarios.takeaway: Label first, then fix the biggest bucket.

quiz.q: Which MAST category contains the failure mode no or incomplete verification?
quiz.explain: MAST has three categories: system design issues, inter-agent misalignment and task verification. No or incomplete verification, incorrect verification and premature termination sit under task verification. Tool failure is not a MAST category. [[r5]]

quiz.q: Match each trace symptom to the MAST category it most likely belongs to.

pairs.l: The agent repeats the same step many times and never stops
An agent ignores another agent's input and drifts off the task
The run ends with a success message and no check that could fail

quiz.explain: Step repetition and unawareness of termination are system design issues. Ignored input and task derailment are inter-agent misalignment. Declaring success without a check, or with a wrong one, is task verification. [[r5]]

flashcards.back: System design issues, inter-agent misalignment and task verification, covering 14 failure modes [[r5]].
A taxonomy built from 150 traces (kappa 0.88), and MAST-Data with 1,600+ annotated traces across 7 frameworks, plus an LLM-as-a-judge annotator [[r5]].

flashcards.front: Which failure is most actionable to fix first in many crews?
flashcards.back: Verification. Use an independent verifier with a clean context and external checks, since a same-context reviewer tends to approve [[r5]][[r4]].
